text: Past performance is not indicative of future results. All investments involve risk, including the possible loss of principal.
This material is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment, legal, or tax advice. Please consult your own advisors before making any financial decisions.
Advisory services are offered through [Firm Name], a registered investment adviser. Fees and expenses will reduce returns.
This communication is intended solely for the individual(s) named above and may contain confidential information. If you received this in error, please notify the sender immediately.
Diversification does not guarantee a profit or protect against loss in a declining market.
Any tax information contained herein is not intended to be used, and cannot be used, for the purpose of avoiding penalties under applicable tax law. Consult a qualified tax professional.
Insurance products are not deposits, are not FDIC insured, are not guaranteed by any bank, and may lose value.
This proposal is not a binding offer and is subject to change without notice. Final terms will be set out in the executed agreement.
Hypothetical or model performance results have inherent limitations and do not reflect actual trading. Results may not reflect the impact of material economic and market factors.
The information provided does not constitute a solicitation to buy or sell any security in any jurisdiction where such solicitation would be unlawful.
Social media posts by advisors must include a disclosure that the content is for educational purposes only and is not personalized investment advice.
Client meeting notes documenting investment recommendations must reference the client's stated risk tolerance and investment objectives on file.
Advisors may not state or imply a guaranteed rate of return on any investment product, including phrases such as 'guaranteed returns' or 'risk-free profit'.
Marketing material may not claim a strategy 'always outperforms the market' or use similarly absolute, unqualified performance language.
Advisors may not reference a client testimonial that implies future clients will achieve similar investment results, without a clear and prominent disclaimer.
Material may not describe an investment as 'safe' or 'no-risk' unless referring specifically to FDIC-insured deposit products within insured limits.
Advisors may not claim exclusive access to an investment opportunity ('only available to my clients') where the product is broadly available through the firm.
Comparative claims against named competitor firms or products are prohibited unless supported by a documented, sourced comparison available on request.
Advisors may not use scarcity or urgency language ('limited time', 'act now before rates change') to pressure a client into an investment decision.
Material may not imply a professional credential or designation the advisor does not currently and verifiably hold.
Advisors may not state that a proposed strategy is endorsed or approved by a government agency or regulator.
Projected or target returns presented without a clearly labeled assumption set (e.g., time horizon, market conditions) are prohibited.
Any performance figures presented must specify the time period covered and whether returns are gross or net of fees.
Performance comparisons to a benchmark index must identify the specific index used and note material differences in composition or risk.
Annualized return figures spanning multiple years must be accompanied by year-by-year performance or a clear reference to where it can be obtained.
Backtested or simulated performance must be clearly labeled as hypothetical and must not be presented alongside actual results without a visual distinction.
Performance data must not selectively present only favorable time periods ('cherry-picking') when longer-term data showing losses is available.
Fee schedules referenced alongside performance figures must be current as of the document's date and must not omit any tier applicable to the client.
Any use of the term 'average annual return' must disclose the calculation methodology (e.g., arithmetic vs. compound annual growth rate).
Proposal letters presenting a target retirement income figure must state the underlying assumptions, including inflation rate and withdrawal rate used.
